paper_metadata.title: Harnessing Bayesian Statistics to Accelerate Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation

summary: This paper introduces Bayesian Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation (BIQAE) and shows, in simulation, that Beta-BIQAE reduces quantum sample complexity relative to IQAE-CP by about 12%–15% for synthetic amplitude estimation and by about 8%–13% for molecular ground-state energy estimation. It also reports quadratic improvement over Classical QAE, with up to 2–3 orders of magnitude lower sample complexity for molecular benchmarks at fixed accuracy, but no physical QPU demonstration.

experiments.description: Iterative quantum amplitude estimation benchmark on arbitrary quantum amplitudes using Beta-BIQAE, compared against IQAE-CP, IQAE-CH, BAE, Classical QAE, Canonical QAE, MLQAE, FQAE, and QAES; evaluated via classical simulation of a mock Grover operator across target accuracies and amplitudes.

problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Iterative quadrant-index tracking; Bayesian credible intervals replace frequentist confidence intervals in BIQAE
